title: Cross-Monitor Agreement Benchmark: Measuring When Multiple Monitoring Approaches Disagree
original_idea: Run 4 monitoring methods (keyword filter, LLM monitor, isolation forest, CUSUM) on all SHADE-Arena public trajectories. Compute pairwise agreement rates and Cohen's kappa. Identify disagreement cases. Analyze whether disagreement predicts lower ensemble performance. Propose ensemble combination rule.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory: inter-monitor agreement reveals complementarity and guides ensemble design. Useful for practical monitoring but the safety-relevant insight is indirect (better ensembles -> better detection).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running 4 different monitoring methods requires setting up each one, which is non-trivial. Keyword filter and CUSUM are simple, but isolation forest needs feature extraction and LLM monitor needs API calls. Feasible but demanding for beginners in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Setting up 4 monitors, computing agreement, analyzing disagreement cases, and proposing ensemble rules is a lot of surface area. Each monitor setup is its own sub-project. Moderately scoped.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
